standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the factorization B = B_n -> ... -> B_0 = A along which the induction runs.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of a smooth morphism through the lifting of objects and morphisms along surjections
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the shape of the data to be lifted, namely y over B, x over A and a morphism y -> phi(x).

core_obligations: Reduce to a factorization (proof lines 2134-2141): given a surjective B -> A and objects y over B, x over A with a morphism y -> phi(x), factor the surjection into finitely many small extensions by the cited factorization lemma and argue by induction on the number of steps.

Induction step (proof lines 2141-2165): split the factorization as B -> B_{n-1} -> A; push y forward to f_*y so that y -> phi(x) factors through f_*y, apply the induction hypothesis to find x_{n-1} -> x and an isomorphism phi(x_{n-1}) -> f_*y over B_{n-1} making the triangle commute, then apply the hypothesis for the small extension B -> B_{n-1} to the composite y -> phi(x_{n-1}) to obtain x_n -> x_{n-1} and phi(x_n) -> y over B.

Conclude (proof lines 2165-2171): the composite x_n -> x_{n-1} -> x together with phi(x_n) -> y are exactly the morphisms required by the definition of smoothness, so phi is smooth for all surjections.
proof_roadmap: Factor an arbitrary surjection into small extensions and induct on the number of factors.
In the induction step push the object forward along the last extension and apply the induction hypothesis and the small extension hypothesis successively.
Assemble the two morphisms required by the definition of smoothness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a morphism of categories cofibred in groupoids is smooth as soon as the lifting condition holds for small extensions (statement lines 2132-2138). The proof (proof lines 2140-2175) factors a general surjection into small extensions and runs an induction in which the induction hypothesis and the small extension case are applied in turn, producing the two morphisms required by the definition. H2: an induction with two inputs, written out in full.
